investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption was also unavailable (No preemption victims found). Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, and all four required evidence fields — orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState — were never written, producing a complete contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled this call cannot return agent identity or VM metadata.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots on those nodes are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for a new remote-agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (4 of 6 are excluded), reducing the effective scheduling pool to exactly the two nodes that are already at capacity. If the affinity were relaxed or more nodes were labeled, scheduling might succeed.

Tertiary — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is set too low relative to concurrent demand from multiple remote-agent probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~8-minute window and all hit the same constraint).

Lower probability — a node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity became NotReady or was cordoned between the last passing run and this run, reducing available VM slots. No history data is available to confirm or deny this (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or quota mechanism would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior probe pod had not yet been cleaned up) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod spec for remote agents does not actually request the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource name or a node taint).
If only one of the three sibling checks failed while the others passed, a shared infrastructure capacity constraint would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would be more likely.

If node affinity rules were recently changed to restrict scheduling to fewer nodes, and that change appears in a commit touching the agent provisioning configuration, that would shift the primary cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration regression — but no such commit is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' signal rather than a timeout failure.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that fires a warning if a remote-agent pod is unscheduled for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it causes a full check failure.

Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods or VMs remain after each probe run, catching leaked resources that would reduce available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots for subsequent runs.

Add a concurrent-capacity eval that attempts to schedule two remote-agent pods simultaneously and verifies both can be placed, validating that the cluster has sufficient VM slots to handle at least the number of simultaneous observability probes.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T20:22–20:27Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent peer-pod VM during this eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, the pod remained pending for ~135–145 seconds until the eval timeout fired, and the runner exited without ever producing the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a surge in concurrent remote agents or a node drain/cordon), the entire remote-agents feature becomes unschedulable. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption was also unavailable (No preemption victims found). Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, and all four required evidence fields — orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState — were never written, producing a complete contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 135s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150248, endedAt=2026-06-30T20:27:06.400Z — confirms the same scheduling failure affected the runtime check.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting and the runner never reaching the evidence-write path.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was captured at all, confirming the probe aborted before any API response was received.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=139790 — the check timed out waiting for the pod, well below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms but above the warningLatencyMs of 240000ms... actually 139790ms is below both thresholds, confirming the runner gave up on the stuck pod before the outage threshold.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled this call cannot return agent identity or VM metadata.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots on those nodes are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for a new remote-agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (4 of 6 are excluded), reducing the effective scheduling pool to exactly the two nodes that are already at capacity. If the affinity were relaxed or more nodes were labeled, scheduling might succeed.

Tertiary — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is set too low relative to concurrent demand from multiple remote-agent probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~8-minute window and all hit the same constraint).

Lower probability — a node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity became NotReady or was cordoned between the last passing run and this run, reducing available VM slots. No history data is available to confirm or deny this (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: The three checks ran sequentially within an 8-minute window and all hit the same constraint. Running them together would reveal whether concurrent probe pods exhaust the available VM slots, pointing to a quota-vs-concurrency issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or quota mechanism would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior probe pod had not yet been cleaned up) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod spec for remote agents does not actually request the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource name or a node taint).
If only one of the three sibling checks failed while the others passed, a shared infrastructure capacity constraint would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would be more likely.

If node affinity rules were recently changed to restrict scheduling to fewer nodes, and that change appears in a commit touching the agent provisioning configuration, that would shift the primary cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration regression — but no such commit is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' signal rather than a timeout failure.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that fires a warning if a remote-agent pod is unscheduled for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it causes a full check failure.

Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods or VMs remain after each probe run, catching leaked resources that would reduce available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots for subsequent runs.

Add a concurrent-capacity eval that attempts to schedule two remote-agent pods simultaneously and verifies both can be placed, validating that the cluster has sufficient VM slots to handle at least the number of simultaneous observability probes.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T20:22–20:27Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent peer-pod VM during this eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, the pod remained pending for ~135–145 seconds until the eval timeout fired, and the runner exited without ever producing the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peerpod nodes have a selector that excludes remote-agent pods, meaning the effective scheduling domain is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a surge in concurrent remote agents or a node drain/cordon), the entire remote-agents feature becomes unschedulable. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — Cluster-level resource quota or limit range on kata.peerpods.io/vm: a namespace or cluster quota may cap the total number of peer-pod VMs, and that cap was reached before the eval ran. This would produce the same Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. The eval never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. The pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck Unschedulable for 135–145 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, no agent identity or runtime response was produced, and the expected-output contract requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message was violated in full. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150248, which is below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 420000 defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185, so the check failed on scheduling error rather than latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes in the production-api cluster, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. All three sibling checks report the same scheduler message, making this the strongest explanation (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, meaning the schedulable node pool for remote agents is structurally limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity for any reason (other running agents, leaked pods from prior eval runs, or a reduction in node count), new pods cannot be placed.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or production workload may have left agent pods running and not yet cleaned up, consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is intended to release resources, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

Lower confidence: A reduction in the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (e.g., node eviction, maintenance, or scaling event) could have reduced available capacity without a code change. No node-level signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm or deny this.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the production-api cluster to determine current VM slot allocation and identify any pods holding slots that should have been released.

Check for leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916); forcibly terminate any stale pods to free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

Determine whether the node pool for remote agents (the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes) has the expected number of VM slots allocated; if slots were reduced, investigate whether a node was evicted, scaled down, or placed into maintenance.
After restoring capacity, re-run the three remote-agents eval checks to confirm they pass and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are collected.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting pod creation, so scheduling failures produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN status rather than a timeout-driven FAIL.

Review whether the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods is intentionally limiting scheduling to only 2 nodes, and whether expanding the eligible node pool is feasible to reduce single-point capacity risk.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and an alternative cause (e.g., node selector misconfiguration or API-level rejection) would need investigation.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks pass on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity problem.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on re-run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
If no pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm are found in the cluster at the time of investigation, the resource exhaustion was caused by a transient burst rather than a persistent leak.

If the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods was recently changed to exclude more nodes, that configuration change would be a contributing cause independent of resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct WARN or FAIL status with a clear capacity message.
Add an eval that detects and reports leaked remote agent pods (pods in Running or Pending state beyond a maximum expected lifetime) to catch cleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are Ready and carrying the expected allocatable resource quantity, alerting on node count or capacity reductions.
Consider a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote agent pods remain after a withCleanup-wrapped probe completes, catching cases where cleanup silently fails.
